title: to, at, in and into
subtitle: go to work / arrive in Madrid / go into a room
summary: Use to for movement to a place, in/at for position, arrive in a town but arrive at a building, and into to enter something.

lesson.heading: go/come/travel to a place
lesson.text: We say **go to** / **come to** / **travel to** a place or an event: go to China, go to work, go to the bank, drive to the airport, return to London, go to a party, be taken to hospital.

examples.text: When are your friends going back **to Italy**?
Three people were injured in the accident and taken **to hospital**.

lesson.heading: Welcome to ... / been to ...
lesson.text: In the same way we say **Welcome to ...**, **a trip to ...**, **a visit to ...**, **on my way to ...** . We also say that somebody **has been to** a place or an event.

examples.text: We had to cancel our **trip to** Paris.
I've **been to** Italy four times, but I've never **been to** Rome.
Amanda has never **been to** a football match in her life.

lesson.heading: get and arrive
lesson.text: We say **get to** a place. With **arrive** we use **in** for a town or country and **at** for other places and events - never *arrive to*.

examples.text: They **got to** the hotel at midnight.
What time did you **get to** the party?
They **arrived in** Madrid / **in** Spain a week ago.
What time did you **arrive at** the hotel / **at** the airport / **at** the party?

lesson.heading: home takes no preposition
lesson.text: We say **go home, come home, get home, arrive home, on the way home**. We do not use *to* before home.

examples.text: I met Lisa **on my way home**.

lesson.heading: into = enter
lesson.text: **go into / get into** = enter a room, a building, a car. The opposite of into is **out of**. With go, get and put we often use **in** instead of into. For buses, trains and planes we say **get on** and **get off**.

examples.text: I opened the door, went **into the room** and sat down.
A bird flew **into the kitchen** through the window.
Every month my salary is paid directly **into my bank account**.
She got **in the car** and drove away.
examples.note: or She got into the car ...

examples.text: She got **out of the car** and went **into a shop**.
You need to **get off** (the train) at the next station.

lesson.text: Cars and taxis: get in / get out of. Buses, trains and planes: get on / get off.

exercises.prompt: Three people were taken ___ hospital after the accident.
exercises.explanation: Movement to a place: be taken to hospital.

exercises.prompt: They arrived ___ Barcelona a few days ago.
exercises.explanation: We arrive in a town or a country (never arrive to).

exercises.prompt: What time do you usually arrive ___ work in the morning?
exercises.explanation: For buildings, places of work and events we say arrive at.

exercises.prompt: We left our luggage ___ the station and went to find something to eat.
exercises.explanation: There is no movement here - the luggage stays in one place, so we use at.

exercises.statement: Welcome in our country! We hope you enjoy your stay.
exercises.explanation: Welcome to our country! We say welcome to, a trip to, a visit to.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with what you did.

pairs.left: A friend stopped her car and opened the door for you.
Your bus came and the doors opened.

pairs.right: I got out of the car.

pairs.left: A taxi stopped and you opened the door.
Your plane landed and the doors were opened.

exercises.prompt: The Amazon flows ___ the Atlantic Ocean.
exercises.explanation: Into shows movement from outside to inside something.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: I opened the door, went into the room and sat down.
exercises.explanation: go/come into a room = enter it.

options: I've been to Italy four times.
I've been in Italy four times.
I've been at Italy four times.
exercises.explanation: We say I've been to a place or an event.

exercises.statement: What time did you get to home last night?
exercises.explanation: What time did you get home last night? We never use to before home.

exercises.prompt: We drove along the main road and then turned ___ a narrow side street.
exercises.explanation: Turn into a street: the car moves from one place inside another.

exercises.prompt: Marcel is French. He has just returned to France after two years ___ Brazil.
exercises.explanation: Return to shows movement, but the two years were spent in Brazil (position).
